newsitem.title: BELGIUM: British officials discuss BSE-free herds with Commission.
newsitem.headline: British officials discuss BSE-free herds with Commission.

text.p: British agriculture ministry officials met their European Commission counterparts on Thursday to discuss a British plan to lift an export ban on beef from herds certified to be free of mad cow disease.
"It's a preliminary technical discussion," a European Commission spokesman said.
"It's a first exchange of information to see if there's scope for lifting the ban," a British spokeswoman added.
Britain recently submitted a working paper to the Commission for exempting grass-fed herds that were certified to be free of the disease, known as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

The permanent secretary in the British Ministry of Agriculture, Richard Packer, told reporters last week after giving evidence to the European Parliament's committee of inquiry into BSE that the document covered the whole of Britain.
But he added that progress could be made on lifting the ban in Northern Ireland, where there was a computerised system for tracking cattle, and the Scottish islands.
The Commission banned British beef exports on March 27 to protect public health after the British government said that the disease could be transmitted to people who ate infected beef.
